newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-GUIMARAES AND BRAGA GO THROUGH TO UEFA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GUIMARAES AND BRAGA GO THROUGH TO UEFA CUP.

text.p: Guimaraes and Braga secured their places in next season's UEFA Cup on Sunday when they drew 0-0 on the final day of the Portuguese first division season.
Salgueiros narrowly missed taking Guimaraes's UEFA Cup place when they missed a penalty in the closing minutes to draw 1-1 away against Farense.
They needed a win to qualify and scored in the 31st minute when Abilio Novais netted a freekick from just outside the area.
Farense equalised in the 64th with a goal by defender Camilo Fernandes.
Salgueiros missed their golden opportunity when Farense keeper Marco Aurelio punched Novais's penalty shot out of harm's way during injury time.
Champions Porto beat bottom-placed Gil Vicente 3-0 at home without much effort after taking the title for a record third successive season a month ago.
Porto set the festive tone when they came on to the pitch with their faces and hair painted in the club's blue and white colours. They left the business of scoring goals until the final 15 minutes.

Polish striker Grzegorz Mielcarksi, who spent much of the season on the bench with injury, opened the scoring with a header in the 75th minute but was swiftly sent off for a second bookable offence when he threw his shirt in the air to celebrate.

Defender Sergio Conceicao scored with a freekick in the 80th minute and five minutes later Gil Vicente midfielder Joao Tuck made the home crowd roar with delight by putting one into the back of his own net.
Portuguese Cup holders Boavista came from behind to beat Sporting 2-1 at home.
Sporting's winger Jose Dominguez finished a counter-attack with the first goal in the 15th minute.
Six minutes into the second half Boavista's Joaquim Martelinho levelled the score and four minutes later Yugoslav striker Simic Sasa scored his team's winner with a rebound.
Benfica finished their worst season in club history with a 1-0 away defeat to Belenenses.

Belenenses scored in the 74th minute with a shot from inside the box by striker Jose Andrade which eluded Belgian keeper Michel Preud'homme, the only player to have played in all 34 first division games this season.
